rows.l: You have up to {max_turns} rounds of interaction. In each round, reply with exactly ONE python code block:
1. Information-gathering code (e.g. inspecting the file) — the execution result is returned to you.
-2. Solution code that writes the modified file to output_path.
-3. Verification code: re-open output_path and print the values you wrote in answer_position,
-   to confirm they are correct before finishing. If they are wrong, fix your code and write again.
-Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct.
+2. Solution code. Structure it as a single function that takes the input and output paths and
+   does ALL the work by reading and computing from the file it is given — then call it once on
+   spreadsheet_path / output_path. This exact final block is re-run on the other graded copies
+   with only the two filenames swapped, so writing it this way makes it recompute correctly on
+   each copy. Follow this shape:
+   ```python
+   def solve(input_path, output_path):
+       import openpyxl
+       wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(input_path)     # read the copy given to you
+       # locate rows/columns by SEARCHING for their header text or using the real used range;
+       # compute every answer value here from what you read — never reuse a number, count, or
+       # position you noticed while inspecting, because it will differ on the other copies.
+       wb.save(output_path)
+   solve("...input.xlsx", "...output.xlsx")        # the paths given above, as plain strings
+3. Verification code: re-open output_path and print the values in answer_position. Before
+   finishing, confirm the values are correct (re-derive at least one from the input a second
+   way), that nothing OUTSIDE answer_position was changed, and that within answer_position you
+   wrote a value ONLY where the answer needs one — a cell that should stay empty or keep its
+   original input must not be overwritten with 0/"". If any check fails, fix the code and write again.
+Reply without a code block ONLY once every check above passes.
If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
